- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecast is flat or rising slowly, overestimate the peak and underreact to supply shocks.  
- After a sharp spike in price, model tends to overshoot and continue upward — cap upward momentum after +10% spike.  
- If supply net is negative and bullish sentiment is high, model underestimates volatility — increase forecast variance or add 3–5% buffer.  
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and model is rising, model is overconfident — reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in early days.  
- If event balance is negative and bullish sentiment is low, model underreacts — add 2–5% upward bias to offset lag.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture late-period volatility — increase forecast variance in last 5–7 days if sentiment swings sharply.  
- When supply net is high and bullish sentiment is low, model underestimates price collapse — add 5–10% downward bias to avoid overconfidence.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated bearish spikes, model tends to lag — adjust forecast to match sentiment reversal 1–2 days ahead.
